title: Polynomial presentation at a closed point of the special fibre
statement: Let $R\to S$ be an essentially finite type homomorphism of commutative rings, with $R$ and $S$ local rings (the map need not be local), and let $\mathfrak m_R$ be the maximal ideal of $R$. Then for some $n\ge0$ there is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ lying over $\mathfrak m_R$ such that $S$ is a localization of a quotient of $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_{\mathfrak n}$. A localization means a ring of fractions $T^{-1}D$ for a subset $T\subset D$ containing $1$ and closed under multiplication; a local ring has exactly one maximal ideal. [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], write $S=W^{-1}(P/I)$ with $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Put $\mathfrak q=(P\to S)^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)$, a prime ideal containing $I$. Every element of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$ maps to a unit of the local ring $S$, so there is a map $P_{\mathfrak q}/IP_{\mathfrak q}\to S$. It is surjective: each fraction $\bar a/w$ defining an element of $S$ is its image, since a lift of $w\in W$ is outside $\mathfrak q$. It is injective: if $a/u$ maps to zero, some $w\in W$ annihilates $\bar a$ in $P/I$; its lift is outside $\mathfrak q$, hence is invertible in $P_{\mathfrak q}$, giving $a/u=0$ modulo $IP_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $S\cong P_{\mathfrak q}/IP_{\mathfrak q}$ as an $R$-algebra. It suffices to find a polynomial ring $Q$ over $R$, a prime $\mathfrak q_Q$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\supseteq\mathfrak q_Q$ over $\mathfrak m_R$, with $Q_{\mathfrak q_Q}\cong P_{\mathfrak q}$ as $R$-algebras. The fraction constructions used here are those in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0AUG, lemma-localization-at-closed-point-special-fibre, proof: first paragraph, reduction to a polynomial local ring; reduction spelled out

proof.text: First record the sufficient condition used in both charts. For a polynomial ring $Q$ and a prime $\mathfrak q_Q$, suppose $\mathfrak q_Q+\mathfrak m_RQ\ne Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] to this proper ideal to choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ containing it. Its contraction to $R$ is proper and contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, so is exactly $\mathfrak m_R$. Because $\mathfrak q_Q\subseteq\mathfrak n$, the ring $Q_{\mathfrak q_Q}$ is a localization of $Q_{\mathfrak n}$: invert the images of all elements of $Q\setminus\mathfrak q_Q$. Both rings of fractions have exactly the same fractions $a/u$ after this inversion, with the same equality relation of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. In particular, if $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_RP\ne P$, take $Q=P$ and $\mathfrak q_Q=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0AUG, lemma-localization-at-closed-point-special-fibre, proof: first paragraph, the proper-ideal case

proof.text: It remains to handle $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_RP=P$. Set $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $B$ be the image of $R\to K$. Its kernel is a proper prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, and $B\cong R/\mathfrak p$ is a local domain with maximal ideal the image of $\mathfrak m_R$: elements outside that image are images of units of $R$. Apply [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] to obtain a valuation ring $V\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ dominating $B$. The inclusion $B\subseteq K$ extends to $\operatorname{Frac}(B)\hookrightarrow K$ by $b/c\mapsto b/c$. Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension] to obtain a valuation ring $A\subseteq K$ with fraction field $K$ dominating $V$. Hence $A$ contains $B$, and $\mathfrak m_A\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$, by contracting first to $V$ and then to $B$. In particular the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_A$ in $R$ is $\mathfrak m_R$. Write $\lambda_j$ for the image of $x_j$ in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0AUG, lemma-localization-at-closed-point-special-fibre, proof: second paragraph, valuation ring dominating the image of R; Tag 00IA, lemma-dominate

proof.text: If all $\lambda_j$ belong to $A$, evaluation gives $P\to A$. Its composition into $K$ has kernel $\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_RP$ is contained in the proper inverse image of $\mathfrak m_A$, contrary to the remaining case. Thus some $\lambda_j$ is outside $A$, and is nonzero. Choose a nonzero pivot $\lambda_i$ for which $\lambda_i^{-1}\in A$ and every $\lambda_j/\lambda_i\in A$ as follows. Start with one coordinate outside $A$, whose inverse is in $A$ by [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Process the other coordinates in order. Keep the pivot if the next coordinate divided by it belongs to $A$ (in particular if that coordinate is zero). Otherwise replace it by that coordinate: the old pivot divided by the new one is in $A$ by the same valuation-ring alternative. Multiplying previously obtained ratios and the old inverse by this ratio preserves all required memberships. Finite induction supplies the claimed pivot, without a value-group theorem. This is also why the remaining case cannot occur for $n=0$.

proof.text: The map $Q\to K$ from Step 5 takes $y_0$ to $\lambda_i^{-1}$ and $y_j$ to $\lambda_j/\lambda_i$, all in $A$ by Step 4; the coefficients also lie in $A$. By the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] it factors through $Q\to A$. Its kernel as a map to $K$ is $\mathfrak q_Q$: an element has zero residue in $P_{\mathfrak q}$ precisely when it belongs to $\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $\mathfrak q_Q$ and $\mathfrak m_RQ$ lie in the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_A$. That inverse image is proper because $1\notin\mathfrak m_A$. Therefore $\mathfrak q_Q+\mathfrak m_RQ\ne Q$, and the criterion in Step 2 applies to this new chart.

source.place: Tag 0AUG, lemma-localization-at-closed-point-special-fibre, proof: last paragraph, the new prime has a specialization in the special fibre

proof.text: We now have in either case an $R$-algebra isomorphism $Q_{\mathfrak q_Q}\cong P_{\mathfrak q}$, and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\supseteq\mathfrak q_Q$ of $Q$ contracting to $\mathfrak m_R$. Let $J$ be the ideal of $Q_{\mathfrak q_Q}$ corresponding to $IP_{\mathfrak q}$, and let $J_0$ be its inverse image in $Q_{\mathfrak n}$. After inverting the images of $Q\setminus\mathfrak q_Q$, the extension of $J_0$ is $J$: if $a/u\in J$ with $a\in Q_{\mathfrak n}$ and $u$ inverted, then $a=u(a/u)\in J_0$. The canonical fraction map consequently gives $S\cong Q_{\mathfrak q_Q}/J\cong T^{-1}(Q_{\mathfrak n}/J_0)$, where $T$ is the image of the multiplicative subset generated by $Q\setminus\mathfrak q_Q$. Surjectivity is the representation by fractions; injectivity is the same cross-multiplication criterion in the quotient. These are exactly the localization definitions [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Rename the $n$ variables of $Q$ as $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. This proves the statement, including the $n=0$ case handled in Step 2.
